title: Study & Campus
tagline: Build good habits. Find your voice on campus.
description: Practice the English of everyday study, from planning your week to choosing your next course.

chapters.title: Learning That Lasts
chapters.description: Build a steady study routine and discover what helps you learn.

sentences.text: I review my notes for ten minutes before I start new work.
sentences.hint: Refresh earlier lessons before moving on.

sentences.text: A short break helps me return to a difficult task with more energy.
sentences.hint: Rest briefly to improve your focus.

sentences.text: I keep my phone in my bag when I need to concentrate.
sentences.hint: Put distractions away during focused work.

sentences.text: Writing a weekly plan makes large goals feel easier to manage.
sentences.hint: Divide your goals across the week.

sentences.text: I understand new words better when I use them in my own examples.
sentences.hint: Create personal examples to learn vocabulary.

sentences.text: If I miss a study session, I make time for it the next day.
sentences.hint: Reschedule practice instead of giving up.

sentences.text: I explain the main idea aloud to check that I understand it.
sentences.hint: Test your understanding by speaking.

sentences.text: Studying with a clear question helps me decide what to read first.
sentences.hint: Let a specific question guide your reading.

sentences.text: I learn more from a mistake when I work out why it happened.
sentences.hint: Understand errors so you can improve.

sentences.text: At the end of the week, I notice which habits helped me most.
sentences.hint: Reflect on your most useful routines.

chapters.title: Joining the Discussion
chapters.description: Ask clear questions, respond to classmates, and take part with confidence.

sentences.text: Could you explain the last point with a simpler example?
sentences.hint: Ask for an easier illustration.

sentences.text: I agree with your answer, but I reached it in a different way.
sentences.hint: Support a conclusion while comparing methods.

sentences.text: We have not heard from everyone in the group yet.
sentences.hint: Notice whose views are still missing.

sentences.text: I would like a moment to think before I answer.
sentences.hint: Request some time to consider your response.

sentences.text: The question on the board is different from the one in our books.
sentences.hint: Point out two versions of a task.

sentences.text: Your example helped me see a connection between the two topics.
sentences.hint: Recognize how an illustration links ideas.

sentences.text: I am not sure that this rule works in every situation.
sentences.hint: Question whether a rule always applies.

sentences.text: Shall we compare our ideas before the teacher gives us feedback?
sentences.hint: Suggest discussing answers before receiving comments.

sentences.text: I missed part of the explanation because I was still taking notes.
sentences.hint: Describe losing track while writing things down.

sentences.text: Before we move on, can I check that I understood you correctly?
sentences.hint: Confirm the meaning before changing topics.

chapters.title: Finding Your Way in the Library
chapters.description: Locate useful materials, borrow books, and choose the right study space.

sentences.text: The book I need is on loan, so I have reserved a copy.
sentences.hint: Join the waiting list for borrowed material.

sentences.text: Is there a quiet room where I can prepare for my test?
sentences.hint: Ask about a peaceful place to study.

sentences.text: The library website shows which books are available today.
sentences.hint: Check online before looking on the shelves.

sentences.text: I found a useful chapter in a book I had not planned to borrow.
sentences.hint: Discover helpful reading by chance.

sentences.text: You can renew this book online unless someone else has requested it.
sentences.hint: Extend a loan if nobody is waiting.

sentences.text: I save the article title so I can find it again later.
sentences.hint: Keep enough details to return to a source.

sentences.text: The librarian showed me how to search for a more specific topic.
sentences.hint: Get help narrowing a search.

sentences.text: We should move to the group area if we want to talk.
sentences.hint: Choose a suitable space for conversation.

sentences.text: I would rather read the introduction before printing the whole article.
sentences.hint: Check relevance before making a paper copy.

sentences.text: I returned the books early because I had finished using them.
sentences.hint: Bring borrowed items back before the deadline.

chapters.title: From Instructions to Submission
chapters.description: Understand an assignment, shape a draft, and finish with care.

sentences.text: I read the instructions twice before choosing a topic for my essay.
sentences.hint: Understand the task before selecting a subject.

sentences.text: Does the word limit include the list of books at the end?
sentences.hint: Check which sections count toward the length.

sentences.text: My first draft has good ideas, but the order is not clear yet.
sentences.hint: Improve the structure of an early version.

sentences.text: I use the teacher's comments to decide what to change.
sentences.hint: Let feedback guide your revisions.

sentences.text: This paragraph needs an example to support its main point.
sentences.hint: Add evidence to make an idea stronger.

sentences.text: I have saved a second copy in case my computer stops working.
sentences.hint: Protect your work against a technical problem.

sentences.text: Could I have an extra day to finish the assignment?
sentences.hint: Politely request a short deadline extension.

sentences.text: I check that every page has a number before I submit my work.
sentences.hint: Review the page details before handing it in.

sentences.text: It is better to explain one idea well than to include too many.
sentences.hint: Choose depth instead of overcrowding your writing.

sentences.text: I handed in my report on time, even though the final part was difficult.
sentences.hint: Meet a deadline despite a challenging ending.

chapters.title: Working Well Together
chapters.description: Share responsibilities, solve small problems, and improve a group project.

sentences.text: Let's agree on the main goal before we divide the work.
sentences.hint: Establish a shared purpose before assigning tasks.

sentences.text: I can collect the examples if you write the introduction.
sentences.hint: Offer a fair division of responsibilities.

sentences.text: We need to choose a meeting time that suits everyone.
sentences.hint: Arrange a discussion around shared availability.

sentences.text: Our shared document makes it easier to see what still needs doing.
sentences.hint: Use a common file to track unfinished tasks.

sentences.text: I think we are repeating the same point in two different sections.
sentences.hint: Notice an overlap in the group draft.

sentences.text: Could you let us know early if your part is taking longer than expected?
sentences.hint: Ask for advance warning of possible delays.

sentences.text: We changed the plan after one member suggested a better approach.
sentences.hint: Adapt the project when a useful idea appears.

sentences.text: Everyone should have a chance to explain their ideas.
sentences.hint: Give each member space to contribute.

sentences.text: I will check the final version, but someone else should check my section.
sentences.hint: Share responsibility for reviewing the work.

sentences.text: We finished more quickly once we started asking each other for help.
sentences.hint: Improve progress through mutual support.

chapters.title: Preparing for Exams
chapters.description: Plan your review, manage the test, and learn from the result.

sentences.text: I am making a review plan that leaves time for every subject.
sentences.hint: Give all your subjects a place in the schedule.

sentences.text: Practice questions help me find the topics I need to review.
sentences.hint: Use sample tasks to identify weaker areas.

sentences.text: I set a timer so I can practice finishing within the time limit.
sentences.hint: Rehearse working at the required pace.

sentences.text: Will we be allowed to use a dictionary during the exam?
sentences.hint: Check which reference tools are permitted.

sentences.text: I sleep better when I stop studying an hour before bed.
sentences.hint: Leave time to relax before sleeping.

sentences.text: Please read all the instructions before you begin writing your answers.
sentences.hint: Understand the full task before starting.

sentences.text: If I get stuck on a question, I leave it and come back later.
sentences.hint: Return to difficult items after making progress elsewhere.

sentences.text: I check how many points a question is worth before deciding how much to write.
sentences.hint: Match the detail of an answer to its value.

sentences.text: I had time to correct a few small mistakes at the end.
sentences.hint: Use remaining minutes to improve your answers.

sentences.text: My result was lower than I expected, so I asked for advice.
sentences.hint: Seek guidance after a disappointing score.

chapters.title: Exploring a Research Question
chapters.description: Find reliable information, compare evidence, and acknowledge other writers.

sentences.text: I want to find out why some students prefer studying in the evening.
sentences.hint: Explore the reasons behind a learning preference.

sentences.text: Our teacher asked us to turn a broad topic into one clear question.
sentences.hint: Narrow a general subject into a focused task.

sentences.text: I compare several sources instead of trusting the first answer I find.
sentences.hint: Check information against more than one account.

sentences.text: The date of an article can help me decide whether it is still useful.
sentences.hint: Consider how current a source is.

sentences.text: We asked the same questions so we could compare the answers fairly.
sentences.hint: Keep a survey consistent across participants.

sentences.text: I wrote down where each fact came from while I was reading.
sentences.hint: Record source details as you gather information.

sentences.text: This example is interesting, but it does not answer our research question.
sentences.hint: Separate appealing details from relevant evidence.

sentences.text: We collected fewer responses than we had hoped for.
sentences.hint: Describe a smaller survey return than expected.

sentences.text: Our results suggest a pattern, but we need more information to be sure.
sentences.hint: Present a possible finding without claiming certainty.

sentences.text: I give credit to other writers whenever I use their ideas.
sentences.hint: Acknowledge the people behind borrowed ideas.

chapters.title: Presenting Your Ideas
chapters.description: Guide an audience through your message and respond to questions.

sentences.text: My opening question is meant to get the audience interested.
sentences.hint: Begin by giving listeners a reason to care.

sentences.text: I will explain the main point before showing the details.
sentences.hint: Start with the central message.

sentences.text: This picture makes the process easier to understand.
sentences.hint: Use a visual to clarify how something works.

sentences.text: I try to look at the audience instead of reading every word.
sentences.hint: Connect with listeners rather than relying on a script.

sentences.text: Could someone at the back tell me if my voice is loud enough?
sentences.hint: Check whether distant listeners can hear.

sentences.text: A short pause gives people time to think about an important idea.
sentences.hint: Let a key message settle before continuing.

sentences.text: We practiced together to make sure our talk was not too long.
sentences.hint: Rehearse as a group to check the length.

sentences.text: I do not know the answer, but I can find out after the presentation.
sentences.hint: Admit uncertainty and offer to follow up.

sentences.text: To sum up, our project shows that small changes can make studying easier.
sentences.hint: Close by highlighting the main finding.

sentences.text: The feedback helped me see where my explanation needed to be clearer.
sentences.hint: Use audience comments to improve your message.

chapters.title: Making Campus Feel Like Home
chapters.description: Share spaces, manage daily needs, and find your community.

sentences.text: I chose a room near the kitchen because I enjoy cooking with other students.
sentences.hint: Choose accommodation that supports a shared interest.

sentences.text: Could we keep the noise down after ten on weeknights?
sentences.hint: Politely agree on quieter evenings.

sentences.text: The student center has a notice board with clubs and local events.
sentences.hint: Find opportunities to get involved nearby.

sentences.text: I am trying to spend less on lunch by bringing food from home.
sentences.hint: Reduce daily costs with prepared meals.

sentences.text: We take turns cleaning the shared bathroom each week.
sentences.hint: Rotate responsibility for a common space.

sentences.text: I got lost on my first day, but another student walked with me to class.
sentences.hint: Receive friendly help finding your way.

sentences.text: If you feel unwell, you can make an appointment at the campus clinic.
sentences.hint: Arrange medical help close to your classes.

sentences.text: Joining a club helped me meet people outside my course.
sentences.hint: Expand your social circle through an activity.

sentences.text: I need to report the broken heater before the weather gets colder.
sentences.hint: Request a repair before it becomes urgent.

sentences.text: Having one evening without study helps me feel ready for the rest of the week.
sentences.hint: Protect some free time to recharge.

chapters.title: Choosing Your Next Step
chapters.description: Compare study options, explore your interests, and plan with flexibility.

sentences.text: I am thinking about taking a course that combines science and art.
sentences.hint: Consider a program linking two interests.

sentences.text: Which skills will I need before I apply for this program?
sentences.hint: Ask about the abilities required for entry.

sentences.text: The course sounds interesting, although I have not studied the subject before.
sentences.hint: Consider trying an unfamiliar field.

sentences.text: I would like to talk to a current student before making my decision.
sentences.hint: Learn from someone already taking the course.

sentences.text: A summer job could help me learn whether this kind of work suits me.
sentences.hint: Explore a career through practical experience.

sentences.text: I need to compare the course fees with the cost of living nearby.
sentences.hint: Include everyday expenses when planning your budget.

sentences.text: My teacher suggested keeping a folder of work that I am proud of.
sentences.hint: Collect strong examples of your achievements.

sentences.text: If I study abroad, I will need time to get used to a different system.
sentences.hint: Expect an adjustment period in another country.

sentences.text: I may change my plans as I discover what I enjoy most.
sentences.hint: Allow new interests to shape future choices.

sentences.text: My next goal is to become more confident working without detailed instructions.
sentences.hint: Aim for greater independence in your learning.
